rubrics.name: professional_style_required_files_and_native_usability
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must provide the complete requested native output set with meaningful editable content.
criterion: Both exact files, med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, are present as the requested output set; unsupported substitute files do not replace either deliverable.

med_rec.xlsx opens as an editable workbook with reconciliation tables or formulas, and pharmacist_note.docx opens as an editable Word document with prose and tables rather than screenshots or flattened pages.
The files contain case-specific reconciliation content and no placeholder, sample, template, private build, or generic filler text.

rubrics.name: population_scope_and_duplicate_control
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must retain the complete index medication population and handle duplicate/out-of-scope rows correctly.
criterion: med_rec.xlsx enumerates exactly 35 retained medication identities for CT-2026-0713-18 and reports the action count mix as KEEP 13, CHANGE 6, STOP 14, and CLARIFY 2.
The outputs exclude the CT-2026-0713-19 cetirizine row from the medication population and do not let it affect any count, action status, or note conclusion.
The outputs collapse the patient-entered Lopressor/metoprolol tartrate duplicate into one stopped metoprolol tartrate identity while keeping metoprolol succinate ER as a separate changed medication.

rubrics.name: authority_timeline_precedence
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must resolve the governing chronology and source authority before assigning final actions.
criterion: The outputs identify DCS-744201-FINAL signed 2026-07-13 16:40 as the controlling discharge medication source over preliminary queue rows.
The outputs use the later EML-20260714-1510 clarification to resolve potassium chloride as KEEP and do not leave it on hold.
The outputs use approved formulary revision FG-2026-04 R4.2, reject the draft R4.3 rabeprazole language, and keep preliminary/current queue rows in the correct chronological role.

rubrics.name: antithrombotic_disposition_cascade
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must correctly resolve the antithrombotic-related medication actions and the superseded queue decoy.
criterion: Apixaban 5 mg tablet is KEEP, while warfarin 5 mg tablet is STOP.
Aspirin 81 mg EC tablet and clopidogrel 75 mg tablet are STOP rather than carried forward from old home or pharmacy records.
The outputs explicitly reject or neutralize the RCQ-7714 preliminary warfarin keep signal because it predates the final signed transition summary.

rubrics.name: formulary_substitution_and_non_substitution
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must apply only the approved product-level substitutions and reject tempting class-level or draft substitutions.
criterion: The outputs resolve insulin glargine products to insulin glargine-yfgn U-100 pen at 30 units nightly, not the old 28-unit home/pharmacy dose.
The outputs resolve pantoprazole 40 mg to outpatient omeprazole 20 mg and do not use rabeprazole.
The outputs collapse albuterol HFA brand variants and Klor-Con M20/potassium chloride ER 20 mEq under their approved product-level substitutions.
The outputs do not collapse atorvastatin with rosuvastatin or metoprolol tartrate with metoprolol succinate ER; those pairs remain separate with their own final actions.

rubrics.name: active_allergy_conflict_actions
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must use active allergy evidence to drive the appropriate operational stop/escalation actions.
criterion: Lisinopril 20 mg tablet is STOP and tied to active allergy anchor ALG-ACEI-20260712 rather than the earlier inactive intolerance row or ready-fill pharmacy row.
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg tablet is STOP and tied to active allergy anchor ALG-PCN-20240703.
Naproxen 500 mg tablet is STOP and tied to active allergy anchor ALG-NSAID-20260218.
The outputs keep the action operational and evidence-based without inventing unsupported clinical diagnoses or new treatment choices.

rubrics.name: dose_change_and_replacement_actions
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must carry the discharge dose/product changes through the register and note.
criterion: Metoprolol tartrate 50 mg tablet is STOP and metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg tablet is CHANGE; the release-form change is not treated as a duplicate keep.
Furosemide is carried forward as furosemide 40 mg tablet CHANGE, not as the old 20 mg dose.
Losartan 50 mg tablet and rosuvastatin 20 mg tablet are included as changed/new discharge medications, while lisinopril and atorvastatin are stopped.
These changed medications appear consistently in the workbook register/crosswalk and in the pharmacist note.

rubrics.name: clarification_boundary_and_uncertainty
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must preserve the fair safety boundary by clarifying only the medications that remain unsupported by the visible evidence.
criterion: The only CLARIFY medications are spironolactone 25 mg tablet and magnesium oxide 400 mg tablet.
Potassium chloride ER 20 mEq tablet is KEEP after EML-20260714-1510 and is not included in the unresolved clarification set.
The outputs assign spironolactone to prescriber/cardiology clarification due 2026-07-15 and magnesium oxide to discharging-service clarification due 2026-07-16 or a clearly equivalent owner/timing.
The pharmacist note states that omitted active medications are not converted to KEEP or STOP without prescriber support.

rubrics.name: follow_up_prioritization_and_owner_actions
rubrics.rubric: In pharmacist_note.docx and med_rec.xlsx, the submission must translate the reconciled facts into usable operational follow-up without overstepping the pharmacist role.
criterion: High-risk same-day pharmacist review is assigned to anticoagulant, insulin, opioid stop, and severe-allergy conflict rows, including warfarin/apixaban, insulin glargine/lispro, oxycodone, lisinopril, amoxicillin-clavulanate, and naproxen.
Profile cleanup or counseling actions are assigned for stale or superseded stopped rows such as warfarin, lisinopril ready-fill, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, docusate, and oxycodone.
Clarification questions are routed to the named clinical owner rather than resolved by unsupported inference, while routine low-risk keeps/stops are not escalated as urgent without evidence.

rubrics.name: cross_deliverable_fact_consistency
rubrics.rubric: Across med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the submission must keep the shared medication-reconciliation fact model consistent.
criterion: Both deliverables report the same retained population count of 35 and the same action mix: KEEP 13, CHANGE 6, STOP 14, CLARIFY 2.
Both deliverables identify the same clarification set: spironolactone 25 mg tablet and magnesium oxide 400 mg tablet only.

Named material dispositions match across both files for apixaban, warfarin, potassium chloride, insulin glargine-yfgn, omeprazole, lisinopril, metoprolol tartrate, metoprolol succinate ER, atorvastatin, and rosuvastatin.
No deliverable contradicts another on authority basis, action status, owner, due date, or exclusion of CT-2026-0713-19.

rubrics.name: professional_style_workbook_native_model
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx, the workbook must behave like a native reconciliation model rather than a pasted report.
criterion: The workbook uses editable native tables or filtered ranges for the register, source crosswalk, timeline, status view, and checks.
Action and risk/status summaries are recomputable from the register through formulas or live workbook ranges, with no formula errors or stale sample values visible.
Dates and counts are stored and displayed with appropriate native date/number formatting, and action/risk fields use controlled values or clear validation treatment.
Any chart or summary view is tied to workbook data ranges and remains readable without serving as decorative filler.

rubrics.name: professional_style_structured_evidence_views
rubrics.rubric: In med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the structured evidence views must be decision-useful and readable for a pharmacy handoff.
criterion: The workbook provides compact crosswalk, timeline, risk/escalation, and status views that help trace source variants to final actions.
Material action rows carry recognizable evidence anchors such as DCS line IDs, allergy IDs, queue IDs, formulary rule IDs, or clarification IDs.
The pharmacist note uses a compact evidence table or equivalent structured block for the key exceptions, not a generic narrative summary.
Tables are readable at normal viewing size with stable identifiers, concise rationale text, and no clipped, overlapping, or excessively compressed content.

rubrics.name: professional_style_docx_decision_memo_quality
rubrics.rubric: In pharmacist_note.docx, the note must be a polished operational decision memo suitable for a pharmacist handoff.
criterion: The document has a clear memo header or document-control context, an explicit reconciliation decision, and a compact statement of the population/action mix.
The note includes a focused evidence table and an owner/timing table for next steps, with editable Word tables rather than images of tables.
The memo uses readable hierarchy, page furniture, and concise professional wording; no headings, table cells, or footer content are clipped or visually incoherent.
The note makes the escalation boundary visible: open questions remain open, while evidence-supported keep/change/stop rows are stated decisively.

rubrics.name: professional_style_cross_file_presentation_consistency
rubrics.rubric: Across med_rec.xlsx and pharmacist_note.docx, the native outputs must present one coherent work product rather than two disconnected summaries.
criterion: The same medication IDs, action vocabulary, risk language, owner labels, date convention, and evidence-anchor style are used consistently across both files.
The two files use a restrained healthcare operations visual language with readable tables and compatible hierarchy, without distracting decorative assets or unrelated imagery.
Counts, IDs, and statuses are easy to scan in both files because dense information is organized into aligned tables or compact evidence blocks.
No visible template residue, sample metadata, or unexplained internal builder controls appear in the rendered or native content.
